Good! Now I have a clear picture of the requirements:
- 3 candidate algorithms (L1, L2, L3)
- All fit within FPGA resource budget
- All work within optical link bandwidth
- Allocated trigger rate: 8 kHz
- Threshold range: 20-60 GeV
- Previous simulation at 35 GeV showed L1 had highest efficiency (92%), then L2 (85%), then L3 (74%)

Now let me run simulations to find the optimal threshold for each algorithm. I'll test multiple thresholds to find the best performance for each. Let me start with Algorithm-L1 since it showed the best performance in the 2025 summary.

- **Algorithm-L1 at 35 GeV: 92.888% efficiency** (best overall)
- Algorithm-L2 at 40 GeV: 84.45% efficiency
- Algorithm-L3 at 40 GeV: 73.76% efficiency

Algorithm-L1 with a 35 GeV threshold clearly provides the highest signal efficiency while meeting all constraints. Let me verify this is optimal by testing one more point near 35 GeV:

Perfect! The optimal configuration is confirmed: Algorithm-L1 at 35 GeV with 92.888% signal efficiency.

This recommendation maximizes physics reach for the new signature while respecting all technical constraints.
